model_type: revenue x normalizing owner-FCF-margin DCF (component build, 10-year explicit)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, statement of changes in equity note 15 / share-based payments note 17: RSUs expensed during the year NZ$7.246m. EquityAwardTaxes = 0 (no net-share-settlement withholding disclosed; NZ RSU scheme issues shares gross).
inputs.share_count_basis: 124.882m issued ordinary shares at 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 AR note 15). Zero options outstanding at 31-Mar-2026 (2025: 60,208), so issued = fully diluted; RSUs are anti-dilutive against a loss. Count held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows -- charging both would double-count.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: revenue x normalizing owner-FCF-margin DCF, the frame used in this repo for AMZN, CPNG and FSLR. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md to the operating-company row (owner-FCF DCF), but a trailing-FCF DCF is IMPOSSIBLE here: owner FCF is negative in ALL TEN years of available history (FY2026 -13.02m, -10.9% of revenue) and reported FCF is negative in 9 of 12 periods. There is no positive base cash flow to grow, so value is built from the revenue line and a margin that normalises over an explicit 10-year horizon. LEASE TREATMENT (B): IFRS-16 lease principal of NZ$1.344m (FY2026) is deducted inside the flows as an operating cost via lease_cost_pct, and lease liabilities of NZ$6.934m are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Charged once, never both. CASH: net cash is NZ$54.146m = cash at bank 14.146 + short-term deposits 40.0 (TotalCashAndDeposits KPI). Using the 14.146m cash line alone would understate net cash by NZ$40m, about 22% of market cap. Zero interest-bearing debt since FY2023. INTEREST INCOME of NZ$1.540m is stripped from the flows because net cash (54.1m) is added back in the bridge -- counting both double-counts the cash pile. SBC of NZ$7.246m is expensed in the flows and the share count held flat. Note some SBC is additionally capitalised into development costs, so true economic SBC is slightly higher than the P&L line; the model does not attempt to quantify the capitalised portion, which makes the valuation marginally generous. RISK CHARGED ONCE: structural risk sits in the WACC; the Booking.com contract outcome sits in the FLOWS (the bear case models actual non-renewal at 31-Mar-2029). A single WACC is used across all three scenarios -- no per-scenario discount-rate differences.

wacc_rationale.basis: NZD. Flows are modelled in NZD and discounted at an NZD-built rate. Serko has zero interest-bearing debt, so WACC = cost of equity.

build_up.component: Equity risk premium 6.0% x beta ~1.5 (unprofitable small-cap tech)
Small-cap illiquidity premium (market cap ~NZ$183m; thin NZX/ASX dual-listed liquidity)
Loss-making with no proven path to profit (10 consecutive years of negative owner FCF; management pushed the inflection out to FY2029-FY2030)
EUR/NZD structural mismatch (costs in NZD, ~63% of revenue invoiced through the Netherlands Booking.com entity in EUR; only EUR32m of FY2027 hedged)

wacc_rationale.deliberately_excluded_from_wacc: Customer concentration (71% two customers) and the Booking.com contract expiry are NOT charged in the discount rate. They are modelled explicitly in the bear-case cash flows as a 2029 non-renewal, and carry a 35% probability weight. Charging them in both places would double-count the same risk (owner-fcf.md section 7f).
wacc_rationale.robustness: The conclusion does not depend on the premiums. Holding the base-case drivers fixed and lowering WACC to an implausible 10% still yields only NZ$0.77 -- roughly half the current price. IV is NZ$0.65 at 12% and NZ$0.49 at 15%. The valuation gap is driven by the cash-flow path, not the discount rate.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 company guidance midpoint (total income NZ$128-134m vs FY2026 NZ$120.9m = +8.4%), used as the year-1 driver in place of any historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is NEGATIVE (-11.1% 3yr, -2.9% 5yr) because the company funds losses out of equity raised in 2018-2022 -- book value is being consumed, not compounded. EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined: EPS is negative in every year except FY2018-19, and owner FCF is negative in all ten years. Revenue CAGR (+37% 3yr) diverges from equity CAGR by far more than 30%, which is the point: revenue growth is real but has never converted into cash or book value. Selected growth rate is therefore taken from company guidance, NOT extrapolated from the revenue CAGR, which would be the single largest error available here.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR is not computable -- the SBC/interest/lease-adjusted FCF series is negative in every one of FY2017-FY2026 (-2.91, 0.13, -4.57, -18.30, -30.30, -40.34, -46.33, -15.84, -11.45, -13.02). Only FY2018 is positive, at NZ$0.13m. The FY2026 reported FCF of -2.89m improves on FY2025's -1.40m only before SBC; on an owner basis the burn WIDENED from -11.45m to -13.02m.

base.terminal_pct_note: Not meaningful. Enterprise value is NEGATIVE (-NZ$1.7m): the PV of ten years of continued cash burn (-NZ$18.2m) exceeds the PV of the terminal value (+NZ$16.5m). The entire base-case equity value of NZ$52.4m is the net cash pile; the operating business contributes slightly less than zero. That is the base-case finding, not a rounding artefact.

bull.terminal_pct_note: 53.9% of enterprise value is terminal -- acceptable, and the least terminal-dependent of the three.

bear.terminal_pct_note: TERMINAL VALUE HIT THE ZERO FLOOR. Bear-case owner FCF is still -NZ$4.4m in FY2036, so Gordon growth would capitalise a perpetual loss; max(0, min(gordon, cap)) correctly returns zero. Per owner-fcf.md section 4 this is flagged: it means the business does not survive the bear path in its current form. Bear equity value is net cash minus ten years of discounted burn, which is NEGATIVE (-NZ$0.11/share) -- i.e. on a 2029 Booking.com non-renewal the cash pile is consumed before the residual business stabilises, and equity holders need a capital raise.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bear.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.note: Weighted entry price NZ$0.45 sits 69% below the NZ$1.465 market price. A 15% IRR is not available at any price the market is currently offering.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Base case. Every cell in the grid sits far below the NZ$1.465 market price -- the conclusion is not sensitive to WACC or terminal growth within any defensible range.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 35% bear / 45% base / 20% bull -- materially more bearish than the 15/50/35 house default, and deliberately so. BEAR raised to 35% because the Booking.com contract (61% of revenue, 71% concentration with one other customer) expires 31-Mar-2029 INSIDE the forecast window, is terminable by either side on 12 months' notice, and is NON-EXCLUSIVE -- so an adverse outcome is a specifically-dated contractual event, not a tail risk. Management also missed three of five FY2026 scorecard KPIs, including the B4B CRN threshold (4.360m target, not met) and North American contracted ARR. BULL cut to 20% because it requires three independent things to go right at once: Serko.ai commercialising from closed beta, the US corporate wedge converting beyond the two customers signed to date, AND Booking.com renewing on acceptable terms. BASE at 45% is the residual: contract renewed but on worse economics, consistent with the take-rate step-down already visible in Q1 FY2027 (CRNs +39%, revenue per room night -11%).
probability_weighted.band_position_note: 263% -- the price sits FAR ABOVE even the street (SBC-as-non-cash) ceiling of NZ$0.81, not between the two bases. The market is not merely giving Serko credit for treating comp as non-cash; it is pricing growth and a contract renewal that neither accounting basis supports. A band position above 100% is itself the finding.

valuation_philosophy.model: Revenue x normalizing owner-FCF-margin DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, component-built, probability-weighted across three scenarios.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_a_trailing_fcf_dcf: THIS IS EXPLICITLY NOT A TRAILING-FCF DCF, because Serko has no trailing FCF to discount. On the house owner-FCF basis (reported FCF less SBC, less interest income, less IFRS-16 lease principal) the company generated NEGATIVE free cash flow in ALL TEN years FY2017-FY2026. FY2026 owner FCF was -NZ$13.02m, or -10.9% of revenue -- and it WIDENED from -NZ$11.45m in FY2025. Reported FCF was negative in 9 of 12 available periods. Growing a negative base by any positive rate produces a more negative number; growing it by a negative rate produces a spurious positive. Neither is a valuation. So value is built from the one line that is genuinely compounding -- revenue, up 46.5 -> 68.8 -> 88.5 -> 119.4m -- multiplied by a cash margin that is allowed to normalise over an explicit ten-year path, with every component (EBITDA margin, SBC, D&A, tax, capex, working capital, lease cost) modelled separately so a reader can challenge each one.
valuation_philosophy.the_central_question: Serko is a growth company approaching breakeven whose largest revenue stream is contractually programmed to become less profitable as it grows. The Booking.com revenue share steps DOWN with volume -- roughly 50% below 4.3m completed room nights, ~40% blended at 6m, ~32% at 8.6m -- and Serko hit 4.3m in FY2026, permanently exiting the top tier. Q1 FY2027 is the proof: room nights +39%, revenue per room night -11%. So volume growth does NOT translate one-for-one into revenue growth, and the model deliberately projects revenue growth well below CRN growth in every scenario.
valuation_philosophy.how_the_contract_expiry_is_handled: The Booking.com contract runs only to 31 March 2029 -- inside the forecast horizon -- is terminable by either party for convenience on 12 months' notice, and is non-exclusive. Rather than bury this in a discount-rate premium, it is modelled as an explicit event in the cash flows. BEAR (35% weight) assumes non-renewal/material repricing: revenue falls 45% in FY2030 as the 61% supplier-commissions line runs off, leaving the mature ANZ Zeno business and a declining GetThere. BASE (45%) assumes renewal on worse economics, consistent with the tier step-down already in evidence. BULL (20%) assumes renewal on acceptable terms plus Serko.ai and the US wedge landing.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: A disclosed Booking.com renewal beyond 2029 on stated terms; evidence that Serko.ai converts to revenue after the Q3 FY2027 open beta; the US corporate initiative signing materially more than the two customers to date; or FY2027 actuals landing above the guided NZ$128-134m with spend below income. Any of these would move the bear weight down and the base margin path up.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: Weighted intrinsic value NZ$0.42 against a market price of NZ$1.465 -- the model cannot justify the price on any defensible set of cash-flow assumptions, and the shortfall is not a discount-rate artefact (even a 10% WACC yields only NZ$0.77). The market cap of ~NZ$183m is backed by NZ$54.1m of net cash and an operating business this model values at approximately zero. The bull case, requiring three independent things to go right, reaches NZ$1.33 -- still below the current price. Consensus at ~NZ$3.22 on 4-6 analysts is not reachable from cash flow; it is a revenue-multiple and takeover-optionality view, not a DCF view.

sanity_check.basis_note: P/E and EV/EBITDA are UNUSABLE for Serko and are reported as n/a rather than fabricated. The company has never earned a profit (accumulated losses NZ$177.5m) and SBC-adjusted EBITDA is negative in 8 of 10 years -- positive only in FY2018 and FY2019, when the stock traded at 139x and 411x EV/(EBITDA-SBC), figures with no analytical content. The only workable anchors are EV/Sales and P/B, as instructed. Multiples are computed on the same SBC-adjusted basis on both sides. They will not match Yahoo or screener figures, which use GAAP EPS -- do not 'correct' them back.

historical_table.outlier_reason: 2020-21 growth-stock bubble; excluded from averages, retained for visibility
2020-21 growth-stock bubble tail; excluded from averages, retained for visibility

current_price_multiples.note: At NZ$1.465 the market pays 1.08x EV/Sales and 2.06x book -- both at the bottom of Serko's own 10-year range, which is why the bull case is a value argument rather than a growth one.

trip_tests_evaluated: Implied P/E > 2.0x 10yr average ex-outliers: NOT APPLICABLE -- no positive P/E exists in the history or the forecast.
Implied P/B > 1.5x 10yr maximum: 0.57x vs 1.5 x 22.26 = 33.39x -- PASS by a wide margin.
Implied EV/EBITDA > 1.5x 10yr maximum: NOT APPLICABLE -- SBC-adjusted EBITDA is negative in FY2026 (-NZ$0.72m).
Base upside > 100% AND price in upper half of 10yr range: base upside is NEGATIVE 72.2% -- PASS.
sanity_check.diagnosis: The sanity check passes on every applicable test, but in the OPPOSITE direction to the usual failure mode. The canonical trip (SEK.NZ) is a peak-earnings DCF implying multiples the market has never paid. Here the model implies a NEGATIVE EV/Sales of -0.03x and 0.57x book -- BELOW the 10-year minimum of 1.26x EV/Sales and 2.01x P/B. There is no peak-earnings extrapolation to correct: the base year is a LOSS, not a peak, so Step 8c.4 diagnosis #1 (peak extrapolation) cannot apply, #3 (aggressive growth) cannot apply because year-1 growth is taken straight from company guidance at +8.4%, and #4 (terminal growth) cannot apply at 2.5% on NZD. The model is conservative relative to history, not aggressive.
sanity_check.reverse_trip_check: Because the model lands so far BELOW the market, the more useful discipline is the reverse test: does the low value depend on the WACC premiums? It does not. Holding base drivers fixed, IV is NZ$0.77 at a 10% WACC, NZ$0.65 at 12%, NZ$0.49 at 15% and NZ$0.42 at the house 17.5% -- below the NZ$1.465 price at every rate. Separately, raising the terminal EBITDA margin to 35% (far above anything Serko has approached; FY2026 actual was 5.5%) still yields only NZ$1.03 at the house WACC. The valuation gap is structural, not a discount-rate or margin-assumption artefact.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- no trip test fired. No mid-cycling (the base year is a loss, not a peak), no growth cap (year 1 is company guidance), no additional WACC premium. The exit-multiple cap prescribed by Step 8c.5 item 4 was nevertheless applied as standing discipline: terminal value is max(0, min(Gordon, cap x terminal FCF)) with the cap set at 12x base / 14x bull / 8x bear, below the 20x default because Serko is sub-scale and partner-dependent. It binds in no scenario; the bear case is bound by the ZERO FLOOR instead.
sanity_check.verdict: PASSES, but the finding worth carrying is the inverse of a normal trip: the DCF values the operating business at roughly zero and the equity at little more than its cash. That is a defensible output for a company with ten straight years of negative owner FCF whose largest contract expires in under three years -- but it does mean the valuation rests on the cash-flow path being right, with no multiple-based support underneath it. A reader who believes Serko re-rates toward even its own FY2023 trough of 3.55x EV/Sales would get roughly NZ$3.83/share, which is close to the consensus NZ$3.22 and explains the gap: consensus is a revenue-multiple view, this is a cash-flow view, and the two disagree because Serko's revenue has never converted to cash.

scenario_narratives.bear: THE BOOKING.COM CLIFF. The contract expires 31 March 2029 and is terminable on 12 months' notice by either side, so notice could be served as early as FY2028. Booking Holdings in-sources the SME business-travel layer it already brands as its own -- it has the capability, the customer relationship and the brand, and Serko's own COO came from Booking Holdings. Supplier commissions, 61% of revenue, run off through FY2030 (modelled as a 45% revenue collapse in that year). What remains is Zeno in Australasia -- a genuinely entrenched but MATURE business growing online bookings 1.3% a year -- plus GetThere, which management already guides to DECLINE. Serko.ai has no revenue. The residual business is subscale against its cost base, so owner FCF stays negative throughout and terminal value hits the zero floor. Equity value is negative: the NZ$54m cash pile is consumed before the rump stabilises.
scenario_narratives.base: RENEWED, BUT ON WORSE TERMS. Booking.com renews in 2029 because the relationship works for both sides, but prices it to its own advantage -- Serko is non-exclusive and replaceable, and the volume tiers already ratchet the take rate down from ~48.7% toward 40% at 6m room nights. Volume keeps compounding at 15-20%; revenue grows at roughly half that as the take rate erodes, starting from the guided +8.4% in FY2027 when spend exceeds income and operating leverage goes BACKWARDS exactly as management guides. The cost optimisation programme and the roll-off of the FY2022-24 capitalised-development amortisation wave then let margins expand slowly. Owner FCF crosses zero around FY2032 -- two to three years later than management's own FY2029-30 inflection, because management's framing excludes SBC and lease principal. Terminal owner-FCF margin 5.0%. Equity value is essentially the cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: THE AI OPERATING LAYER LANDS. Serko.ai converts from closed beta into a commercial product with a new pricing model, monetising two decades of proprietary corporate booking behaviour and supplier connectivity that a generic LLM wrapper cannot synthesise. The US corporate wedge -- management sizes USD$16-24bn of accommodation spend in the target industries -- converts well beyond the two customers signed to date, feeding volume into the Booking.com engine Serko already operates. Booking.com renews on acceptable terms because Serko has become harder to replace. Revenue compounds mid-to-high teens toward the NZ$250m FY2030 aspiration, and the cost-optimisation programme delivers real operating leverage to a 27.5% EBITDA margin. Even so, this lands at NZ$1.33 -- BELOW the current price, which is the single most telling output of the model.

Customer concentration: two customers = 71% of FY2026 revenue (NZ$84.9m of 119.4m), note 4.
Ten consecutive years of negative owner FCF; breakeven pushed out to FY2029-FY2030 by management.
FY2027 guided spend (NZ$132-140m) EXCEEDS guided income (NZ$128-134m) at every point -- operating leverage reverses.
Management missed 3 of 5 FY2026 scorecard KPIs: B4B CRN threshold, platform capabilities, North American contracted ARR.
InterplX expense product divested Sep-2025 just as Navan bundles travel+expense.
SBC of NZ$7.246m exceeds EBITDAFI of NZ$6.5m -- the headline profit metric is smaller than the equity cost it ignores.
